sentences.text: The name Orientalosuchus combines the Latin word for 'east' and the Greek word for 'crocodile' to reference its geographic range. This small crocodilian possessed a blunt, rounded snout with teeth that were pointed at the front and blunt at the back. Its nostrils faced upwards and were roughly square-shaped with rounded edges. The upper jaw bones displayed wavy outer edges known as festooning, featuring alternating flaring and constricting. The front part of the lower jaw where the two halves meet extended back to the fifth tooth and was made entirely of dentary bone. The external opening in the lower jaw was very small, only slightly larger than the inner opening. In the upper jaw, there were five premaxillary teeth and thirteen maxillary teeth on each side. The fourth premaxillary tooth was the largest, followed by the third, while the others were much smaller. The maxillary teeth in the upper jaw increased in size until the fifth tooth, which was the largest, before decreasing in size.

The genus Orientalosuchus was described in 2019 based on fossils from at least 29 individuals. Fossils of Orientalosuchus include more postcranial material than any other known member of its group. The preserved skeleton includes most of the spine, ribs, shoulder and pelvic girdles, limbs, and osteoderms.

Fossils of Orientalosuchus were discovered between 2009 and 2012 in the Na Duong Basin in Northeastern Vietnam near the Chinese border. All Orientalosuchus fossils come from the Na Duong Formation, dating from the late Bartonian to Priabonian stages of the Eocene. The genus Orientalosuchus was named by Massonne and colleagues in 2019.

Orientalosuchus was a crocodilian that lived during the Late Eocene in Vietnam. Orientalosuchus inhabited tropical to warm-subtropical freshwater biomes including ponds, anoxic lakes, and swamp forests. Orientalosuchus lived in Vietnam during the Eocene epoch, specifically from the Bartonian to Priabonian stages. The environment where Orientalosuchus lived was a tropical to warm-subtropical swamp containing brooks, shallow ponds, and anoxic lakes. The terrestrial habitat surrounding the aquatic environments was a waterlogged swamp forest. The canopy of the swamp forest where Orientalosuchus lived was estimated to be 35 meters high.

Orientalosuchus was adapted to eat hard-shelled prey like the many turtles found in its habitat. Researchers suggest that Orientalosuchus was likely a generalist feeder due to its broader skull compared to other longirostrine species. Evidence of crocodilian bite marks on turtle shells supports the hypothesis that Orientalosuchus preyed on hard-shelled or armoured animals.
Orientalosuchus could have grown up to 2 meters long. Footprints attributed to Orientalosuchus suggest an animal length of approximately 2 meters, though this may not represent an adult.

Orientalosuchus belongs to the parent group Orientalosuchina. Orientalosuchus is classified within the class Reptilia. The type species of the genus Orientalosuchus is Orientalosuchus naduongensis. Initial phylogenetic analyses placed Orientalosuchus as the closest relative to Krabisuchus.
Orientalosuchus was key to establishing the clade Orientalosuchina, which was initially thought to be early alligatoroids but is now argued to be crocodyloids.
The time range for Orientalosuchus is estimated to be between 41.03 and 33.9 million years ago.

It is debated whether Orientalosuchina belongs at the base of Alligatoroidea or closer to crocodyloids. A 2024 study recovered Orientalosuchina in two different positions: at the base of Alligatoroidea or as a basal branch of Longirostres outside the crocodyloid-gavialoid split.
